creators.name: Heather Barnett
creators.role: Artist and educator; Pathway Leader, MA Art and Science, Central Saint Martins (UAL)
creators.bio: British artist who has worked with the slime mould Physarum polycephalum since 2008 through films, experiments and participatory games about collective intelligence.
creators.why: She uses a brainless single cell as a model for how groups, cities and people make decisions.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、教育者；伦敦艺术大学中央圣马丁学院艺术与科学硕士课程负责人
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，自 2008 年起与多头绒泡菌（Physarum polycephalum）合作，通过影像、实验和参与式游戏探讨集体智能。
creators.why_zh: 她把一个没有大脑的单细胞当作模型，用来思考群体、城市和人如何做决定。

creators.name: Theresa Schubert
creators.role: Artist between media art and bioart; PhD, Bauhaus-University Weimar
creators.bio: Berlin-based artist who builds installations with slime mould, fungi, algae and microbes, often coupled to sensors, simulations and generative sound.
creators.why: Her works turn the growth and metabolism of non-neuronal organisms into inputs for audiovisual systems.
creators.role_zh: 游走于媒体艺术与生物艺术之间的艺术家；魏玛包豪斯大学博士
creators.bio_zh: 柏林艺术家，用黏菌、真菌、藻类和微生物创作装置，常把它们与传感器、模拟程序和生成声音连接在一起。
creators.why_zh: 她的作品把没有神经系统的生物的生长和代谢变成视听系统的输入。

creators.name: AKI INOMATA
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Japanese artist who collaborates with animals such as hermit crabs, bagworms, beavers and octopuses, letting their behaviour shape the finished work.
creators.why: She treats animals as co-authors and asks who the artist is when another species does the making.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家，与寄居蟹、蓑蛾幼虫、河狸、章鱼等动物合作，让它们的行为决定作品的最终形态。
creators.why_zh: 她把动物当作共同作者，追问当另一个物种动手制作时，谁才是艺术家。

creators.name: Tarsh Bates
creators.role: Artist and researcher; PhD in Biological Art, SymbioticA, University of Western Australia
creators.bio: Australian artist whose long-term practice centres on living with the yeast Candida albicans and other organisms, exploring interspecies care and the human body as an ecosystem.
creators.why: Her works make the microbes inside human bodies into visible, living partners.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、研究者；西澳大学 SymbioticA 生物艺术博士
creators.bio_zh: 澳大利亚艺术家，长期与白色念珠菌（Candida albicans）等生物共处创作，探讨跨物种照护以及人体作为生态系统。
creators.why_zh: 她的作品让人体内的微生物成为看得见的、活的伙伴。

creators.name: Dmitry Morozov (::vtol::)
creators.role: Media artist and instrument builder
creators.bio: Russian artist working as ::vtol::, known for robotic sound objects, circuit bending and instruments that run on unusual signals, including his own blood and brain activity.
creators.why: Pushes the idea of a biohybrid instrument to the body itself: blood as a battery, EEG as a control signal.
creators.role_zh: 媒体艺术家、乐器制作者
creators.bio_zh: 俄罗斯艺术家，以 ::vtol:: 为名创作，擅长机器人声音装置、电路改造，以及由非常规信号驱动的乐器，包括他自己的血液和脑电。
creators.why_zh: 把生物混合乐器推进到身体本身：血液作电池，脑电作控制信号。
creators.based_zh: 莫斯科，俄罗斯 / 卢布尔雅那，斯洛文尼亚

creators.name: Bartaku
creators.role: Artist-researcher
creators.bio: Belgian artist-researcher who has worked since 2007 on 'PhoEf', a long inquiry into the photovoltaic effect, making dye-sensitised solar cells from Aronia berries (Baroa belaobara) with scientists at Aalto University.
creators.why: Treats a berry plant and its microbes as co-authors of an energy technology, from edible solar cells to a bio-solar painting.
creators.role_zh: 艺术研究者
creators.bio_zh: 比利时艺术研究者，自 2007 年起进行名为“PhoEf”的光伏效应长期研究，与阿尔托大学的科学家一起用野樱莓（Aronia，他称之为 Baroa belaobara）制作染料敏化太阳能电池。
creators.why_zh: 把一种浆果植物及其微生物当作能源技术的共同作者，从可食用太阳能电池到生物太阳能画作。
creators.based_zh: 布鲁塞尔，比利时 / 赫尔辛基，芬兰

creators.name: Andy Gracie
creators.role: Artist (hostprods), co-founder of Hackteria
creators.bio: British artist whose installations connect robots, AI and living organisms such as fish, crickets, cyanobacteria and fruit flies, often framed as astrobiology experiments.
creators.why: An early practitioner of feedback loops where animals or microbes steer machines and machines try to talk back.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家（hostprods），Hackteria 联合创始人
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，他的装置把机器人、人工智能与鱼、蟋蟀、蓝藻和果蝇等生物连接起来，常以天体生物学实验的形式呈现。
creators.why_zh: 较早探索“动物或微生物操控机器、机器尝试回应”这种反馈回路的实践者。

creators.name: Adam W. Brown
creators.role: Artist; Professor, Michigan State University
creators.bio: American artist whose 're-enactments' use microbiology and chemistry, from gold-making bacteria to bleeding hosts, to question human exceptionalism. He has received four Prix Ars Electronica awards.
creators.why: Stages microbes as historical and alchemical agents inside custom bioreactors, so audiences watch a metabolism perform.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；密歇根州立大学教授
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，以“重演”为方法，借助微生物学和化学，从能产金的细菌到“流血”的圣饼，质疑人类例外论。曾四次获得 Prix Ars Electronica 奖项。
creators.why_zh: 在定制生物反应器中把微生物塑造成历史与炼金术的行动者，让观众看到新陈代谢本身在表演。

creators.name: Anne Marie Maes
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Belgian artist who has run the Bee Laboratory on Brussels rooftops since 2009, building instrumented beehives and bacterial biofilms that monitor urban ecosystems.
creators.why: Turns honeybees and bacteria into living sensors of city pollution, and the hive into an interface.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 比利时艺术家，自 2009 年起在布鲁塞尔屋顶运营 Bee Laboratory，制作装有传感器的蜂箱和监测城市生态的细菌生物膜。
creators.why_zh: 把蜜蜂和细菌变成城市污染的活体传感器，把蜂箱变成界面。

creators.name: Agnes Meyer-Brandis
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: German artist whose 'poetic-scientific' projects mix fieldwork, lab work and fiction, from raising moon geese to making a perfume from a tree's volatile compounds.
creators.why: Designs situations where humans enter another organism's channel of communication, by imprinting or by scent.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家，她的“诗意科学”项目把田野调查、实验室工作和虚构交织在一起，从养育“月球鹅”到用树木的挥发性化合物制作香水。
creators.why_zh: 设计让人进入另一种生物交流通道的情境，通过印随或气味。

creators.name: Robert Root-Bernstein
creators.role: Professor of Physiology, Michigan State University
creators.bio: American physiologist who studies the origins of life, creativity and the links between art and science; long-time collaborator of Adam W. Brown.
creators.why: A scientist who co-authors artworks, bringing origin-of-life chemistry into the gallery.
creators.role_zh: 密歇根州立大学生理学教授
creators.bio_zh: 美国生理学家，研究生命起源、创造力以及艺术与科学的关联；长期与 Adam W. Brown 合作。
creators.why_zh: 一位与艺术家共同署名作品的科学家，把生命起源化学带进展厅。

creators.name: Monika Pocrnjić
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Slovenian artist working with sound, analog electronics and living systems; co-author of Oscillatorium with Robertina Šebjanič.
creators.why: Treats natural oscillations in organisms as material for analog sound electronics.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 斯洛文尼亚艺术家，创作涉及声音、模拟电子和生命系统；与 Robertina Šebjanič 共同创作 Oscillatorium。
creators.why_zh: 把生物体内的自然振荡当作模拟声音电子的素材。
creators.based_zh: 卢布尔雅那，斯洛文尼亚

creators.name: Cyrus Clarke
creators.role: Co-founder and strategy lead, Grow Your Own Cloud
creators.bio: Designer and researcher who co-founded Grow Your Own Cloud in 2018 to store digital data in the DNA of living plants.
creators.why: Turns DNA data storage into public, hands-on scenarios where plants become data centres.
creators.role_zh: Grow Your Own Cloud 联合创始人、战略负责人
creators.bio_zh: 设计师与研究者，2018 年与 Monika Seyfried 共同创立 Grow Your Own Cloud，尝试把数字数据存进活植物的 DNA。
creators.why_zh: 把 DNA 数据存储变成公众可以亲手参与的场景，让植物成为数据中心。

creators.name: Monika Seyfried
creators.role: Co-founder and operations lead, Grow Your Own Cloud
creators.bio: Designer and co-founder of Grow Your Own Cloud, which develops plant-based DNA data storage with scientific advisor Jeff Nivala.
creators.why: Co-authors design fictions and installations that make biological data storage tangible.
creators.role_zh: Grow Your Own Cloud 联合创始人、运营负责人
creators.bio_zh: 设计师，Grow Your Own Cloud 联合创始人，与科学顾问 Jeff Nivala 一起开发基于植物的 DNA 数据存储。
creators.why_zh: 共同创作让生物数据存储变得可感可触的设计虚构与装置。

creators.name: Ori Elisar
creators.role: Designer, Bezalel Academy of Arts and Design graduate
creators.bio: Visual communication designer who trained in microbiology in Eshel Ben-Jacob's lab at Tel Aviv University and studied Hebrew linguistics.
creators.why: Uses the growth of pattern-forming bacteria as a typographic process.
creators.role_zh: 设计师，毕业于 Bezalel 艺术与设计学院
creators.bio_zh: 视觉传达设计师，曾在特拉维夫大学 Eshel Ben-Jacob 实验室接受微生物学训练，并学习希伯来语言学。
creators.why_zh: 把会自组织成图案的细菌生长当作一种字体设计过程。

creators.name: Hideo Iwasaki
creators.role: Professor, Waseda University; founder of the metaPhorest bioaesthetics platform
creators.bio: Cyanobacteria and circadian-clock biologist and paper-cut artist who founded metaPhorest in 2007 as a lab-based platform for biomedia art.
creators.why: Makes the scientist's own study organism, cyanobacteria, the co-author of artworks about how science describes life.
creators.role_zh: 早稻田大学教授，生命美学平台 metaPhorest 创立者
creators.bio_zh: 研究蓝细菌与生物钟的生物学家，也是剪纸艺术家；2007 年在实验室内创立生命美学平台 metaPhorest，推动生物媒体艺术。
creators.why_zh: 让自己作为科学家研究的对象——蓝细菌——成为作品的共同作者，反思科学如何描述生命。

creators.name: Ursula Damm
creators.role: Artist; professor of Media Environments, Bauhaus-Universität Weimar
creators.bio: Media artist who works with swarming midges, fruit flies and generative video to build feedback systems between insects, humans and machines.
creators.why: Treats insect behaviour and sound as live data that people can play with and influence.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家，魏玛包豪斯大学媒体环境教授
creators.bio_zh: 媒体艺术家，用摇蚊群、果蝇和生成式影像构建昆虫、人与机器之间的反馈系统。
creators.why_zh: 把昆虫的行为与声音当作人可以参与、可以影响的实时数据。

creators.name: Mick Lorusso
creators.role: Cross-disciplinary artist
creators.bio: Artist who builds microbial fuel cells, DIY microscopes and shadow theatres to stage microbial communities as energy producers and storytellers.
creators.why: Shows bacteria as collaborators that literally power small public spectacles.
creators.role_zh: 跨学科艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家，用微生物燃料电池、自制显微镜和皮影剧场，把微生物群落呈现为能量生产者和讲故事的角色。
creators.why_zh: 把细菌表现为合作者：它们真正为小型公共演出提供电力。

creators.name: ArtScienceBangalore
creators.role: Art-science lab at the Srishti School of Art, Design and Technology, led by Yashas Shetty
creators.bio: Art-science collective and DIY biolab founded at Srishti with the National Centre for Biological Sciences, known for iGEM-related bioart and mobile public labs.
creators.why: Brings synthetic biology into open, self-built labs where the public can question it.
creators.role_zh: Srishti 艺术设计与技术学院的艺术科学实验室，由 Yashas Shetty 领导
creators.bio_zh: 在 Srishti 与国家生物科学中心（NCBS）合作下成立的艺术科学团体与 DIY 生物实验室，以 iGEM 相关生物艺术和移动公共实验室闻名。
creators.why_zh: 把合成生物学带进开放、自建的实验室，让公众去追问它。

creators.name: Yuichi Oba
creators.role: Biologist, Chubu University
creators.bio: Bioluminescence researcher who led the reconstruction of the ancestral firefly luciferase published in Science Advances in 2020.
creators.why: Provides the molecular science that lets an extinct glow be seen again in a gallery.
creators.role_zh: 中部大学生物学家
creators.bio_zh: 生物发光研究者，主导复原祖先萤火虫荧光素酶的研究，成果于 2020 年发表在 Science Advances。
creators.why_zh: 提供分子生物学基础，让一种已消失的光在展厅中重现。

creators.name: Nelo Akamatsu
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Japanese artist known for sound installations such as Chijikinkutsu, in which magnetised needles in water glasses sound through Earth's magnetism.
creators.why: Turns invisible natural forces and molecules into quiet, perceptible phenomena.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家，以《Chijikinkutsu》等声音装置闻名：水杯中的磁化针借地磁发出声响。
creators.why_zh: 把看不见的自然力与分子变成安静、可被感知的现象。

creators.name: Thomas Feuerstein
creators.role: Artist; lecturer at art universities in Austria and Switzerland
creators.bio: Austrian artist whose 'processual sculptures' run on bacteria, algae and human cell cultures grown with scientists at the University of Innsbruck.
creators.why: He builds sculptures as metabolic machines, turning text, stone or cells into running biological processes.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；在奥地利和瑞士多所艺术大学任教
creators.bio_zh: 奥地利艺术家，他的“过程雕塑”依靠细菌、藻类和人类细胞培养物运转，与因斯布鲁克大学的科学家合作完成。
creators.why_zh: 他把雕塑做成代谢机器，让文字、石头或细胞变成持续运行的生物过程。

creators.name: Zoran Srdić Janežič
creators.role: Sculptor and intermedia artist; PhD researcher at AGRFT, University of Ljubljana
creators.bio: Slovenian sculptor who works with animatronics, 3D design and living tissue; since 2019 he has led the Biobot series with Kapelica Gallery and BioTehna Lab.
creators.why: His Biobot series lets signals from the artist's own reprogrammed neurons shape and move a robot body.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家、跨媒介艺术家；卢布尔雅那大学 AGRFT 博士研究者
creators.based_zh: 卢布尔雅那，斯洛文尼亚
creators.bio_zh: 斯洛文尼亚雕塑家，使用动画机械、三维设计和活体组织创作；自 2019 年起与 Kapelica 画廊和 BioTehna 实验室合作推进 Biobot 系列。
creators.why_zh: 他的 Biobot 系列让由艺术家自身细胞重编程而来的神经元信号去塑造并驱动机器人身体。

creators.name: Cody Lukas
creators.role: Artist working with living systems and scientific collaborators
creators.bio: Artist whose installations question where people draw the line of 'life', made with labs such as the University of Southern Denmark and the OvaCure organoid biobank.
creators.why: He turns lab organoids into partners in a conversation, so visitors meet them as more than research material.
creators.role_zh: 与活体系统和科学合作者一起创作的艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家，作品追问人们把“生命”的界线划在哪里，常与南丹麦大学、OvaCure 类器官生物样本库等机构合作。
creators.why_zh: 他把实验室里的类器官变成对话的一方，让观众不再只把它们看成研究材料。

creators.name: Helen Pynor
creators.role: Artist working with the body, organs and life-death thresholds
creators.bio: Australian artist who works with organs, tissue and medical science; she made The Body is a Big Place with Peta Clancy at SymbioticA and with transplant researchers.
creators.why: She stages living organs as performers to make the slow boundary between life and death visible.
creators.role_zh: 关注身体、器官与生死边界的艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 澳大利亚艺术家，与器官、组织和医学研究者合作；她与 Peta Clancy 一起在 SymbioticA 和器官移植研究者的支持下完成了 The Body is a Big Place。
creators.why_zh: 她让活的器官成为表演者，使生与死之间缓慢的过渡变得可见。

creators.name: Justine Emard
creators.role: Visual artist working with neuroscience, robotics and machine learning
creators.bio: French artist who combines photography, video, robotics and AI; her works draw on data from bees, brains and androids.
creators.why: She uses data from living collectives, such as a bee colony, to animate machines that behave like an organism.
creators.role_zh: 结合神经科学、机器人和机器学习的视觉艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术家，结合摄影、影像、机器人和人工智能；作品数据来自蜜蜂、大脑和仿人机器人。
creators.why_zh: 她用蜂群等活体集体的数据去驱动像生物一样行动的机器。

creators.name: Kathy High
creators.role: Professor of Video and New Media, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
creators.bio: American artist and educator who works with living systems, animal sentience and biotech ethics; she coordinates the NATURE Lab at the Sanctuary for Independent Media.
creators.why: She turns lab procedures on human cells into participatory games that make biology debatable.
creators.role_zh: 伦斯勒理工学院视频与新媒体教授
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家和教育者，关注活体系统、动物感知和生物技术伦理，在 Sanctuary for Independent Media 主持 NATURE Lab。
creators.why_zh: 她把针对人体细胞的实验室流程变成参与式游戏，让生物学成为可以讨论的话题。

creators.name: Tuurm
creators.role: Interactive design studio founded by Zurich University of the Arts graduates
creators.bio: Zurich studio that builds tactile installations for museums and public spaces; its founders made SOMA at ZHdK with FinalSpark.
creators.why: SOMA is an early design study of how touching a living neural computer could feel.
creators.role_zh: 由苏黎世艺术大学毕业生创立的交互设计工作室
creators.bio_zh: 苏黎世的工作室，为博物馆和公共空间制作触觉交互装置；创始人在苏黎世艺术大学与 FinalSpark 合作完成了 SOMA。
creators.why_zh: SOMA 是关于“触摸一台活体神经计算机会是什么感觉”的早期设计研究。

creators.name: Art Orienté Objet
creators.role: Artist duo of Marion Laval-Jeantet and Benoît Mangin
creators.bio: French duo formed in 1991 by Marion Laval-Jeantet and Benoît Mangin, working between ethology, biology and transcultural psychiatry.
creators.why: Their horse-blood performance made cross-species kinship a physical, immunological event.
creators.role_zh: 由 Marion Laval-Jeantet 与 Benoît Mangin 组成的艺术双人组
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术双人组，由 Marion Laval-Jeantet 与 Benoît Mangin 于 1991 年组成，游走于动物行为学、生物学与跨文化精神医学之间。
creators.why_zh: 他们以马血进行的表演，把跨物种的亲缘变成一次身体上的免疫事件。

creators.name: Ken Rinaldo
creators.role: Artist; professor emeritus of art and technology, The Ohio State University
creators.bio: American artist who has built interspecies robotic installations since the late 1980s, in which fish, insects and bacteria steer or switch machines.
creators.why: One of the first artists to hand the controls of a robot to an animal, framing it as interactive art for non-humans.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；俄亥俄州立大学艺术与技术荣休教授
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，自 20 世纪 80 年代末起创作跨物种机器人装置，让鱼、昆虫和细菌来驾驶或开关机器。
creators.why_zh: 最早把机器人的控制权交给动物的艺术家之一，并把它定位为「给非人类的互动艺术」。

creators.name: Garnet Hertz
creators.role: Artist and design researcher; Canada Research Chair in Design and Media Arts, Emily Carr University
creators.bio: Canadian artist and researcher known for critical making, DIY electronics and the cockroach-driven robot he built as a graduate student at UC Irvine.
creators.why: His cockroach-controlled robot is a reference point for insect-as-CPU artworks.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、设计研究者；Emily Carr 大学设计与媒体艺术加拿大研究讲席
creators.bio_zh: 加拿大艺术家与研究者，以批判性制作、DIY 电子，以及他在 UC Irvine 读研时做的蟑螂驾驶机器人而知名。
creators.why_zh: 他的蟑螂控制机器人是「昆虫当 CPU」类艺术作品的参照点。

creators.name: David Bowen
creators.role: Studio artist and educator
creators.bio: American artist who builds robotic and data-driven sculptures, many of them steered by houseflies or by the electrical signals of living plants.
creators.why: His long series of fly- and plant-controlled machines shows how simple organism input can drive drawing, flight, carving and industrial robots.
creators.role_zh: 工作室艺术家、教师
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，制作机器人与数据驱动的雕塑，其中许多由家蝇或活植物的电信号来操控。
creators.why_zh: 他长期的「苍蝇 / 植物操控机器」系列说明：生物最简单的输入，就能驱动绘图、飞行、雕刻乃至工业机器人。

creators.name: Guto Nóbrega
creators.role: Artist; professor at the School of Fine Arts, UFRJ, and coordinator of the NANO lab (Núcleo de Arte e Novos Organismos)
creators.bio: Brazilian artist-researcher whose PhD at the University of Plymouth produced plant-machine hybrids read through galvanic response sensors.
creators.why: An early artist to treat a living plant as the sensing core of a robotic creature.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；里约热内卢联邦大学美术学院教授，NANO 实验室（艺术与新有机体中心）负责人
creators.bio_zh: 巴西艺术家、研究者，在普利茅斯大学的博士研究中做出以皮电传感读取的植物—机器混合体。
creators.why_zh: 较早把活植物当作机器人生物体「感知核心」的艺术家。

creators.name: Ken Goldberg
creators.role: Roboticist and artist; professor, UC Berkeley
creators.bio: Robotics researcher and artist who pioneered internet-controlled robots in the mid-1990s, including The Telegarden with Joseph Santarromana.
creators.why: The Telegarden made a living garden the shared object of a remote online community.
creators.role_zh: 机器人学者、艺术家；加州大学伯克利分校教授
creators.bio_zh: 机器人研究者与艺术家，90 年代中期开创了互联网遥控机器人，包括与 Joseph Santarromana 合作的 The Telegarden。
creators.why_zh: The Telegarden 让一座活的花园成为远程网络社群共同照料的对象。

creators.name: Céleste Boursier-Mougenot
creators.role: Artist and composer
creators.bio: French artist and trained composer who builds installations where living systems, water or traffic generate music; he represented France at the 2015 Venice Biennale.
creators.why: His finches playing electric guitars is a widely seen example of animals as unscripted musicians.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、作曲家
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术家，作曲出身，创作由生命系统、水流或交通来生成音乐的装置；2015 年代表法国参加威尼斯双年展。
creators.why_zh: 他让斑胸草雀弹电吉他的作品，是「动物作为即兴乐手」最广为人知的例子之一。

creators.name: Laura Beloff
creators.role: Artist and researcher; professor, Aalto University
creators.bio: Finnish artist-researcher working on wearables, hybrid ecologies and art with living organisms, from plants to ticks and protocells.
creators.why: She uses artistic experiments to question how humans can sense signals of other species.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、研究者；阿尔托大学教授
creators.bio_zh: 芬兰艺术家、研究者，研究可穿戴物、混合生态以及与活体生物（从植物到蜱虫、原细胞）合作的艺术。
creators.why_zh: 她用艺术实验追问：人类怎样才能感知其他物种发出的信号。

creators.name: Tosca Terán
creators.role: Interdisciplinary artist and performer (Nanotopia)
creators.bio: Canadian-Mexican artist who performs and installs sound and XR works driven by the bio-electrical activity of mycelium, slime mould and plant roots.
creators.why: Shows how living fungi can act as a live controller for synthesizers, visuals and VR worlds.
creators.role_zh: 跨学科艺术家、表演者（艺名 Nanotopia）
creators.bio_zh: 加拿大 / 墨西哥艺术家，用菌丝、黏菌和植物根系的生物电活动驱动声音与 XR 作品，进行表演和装置创作。
creators.why_zh: 展示了活真菌如何作为合成器、影像和 VR 世界的实时控制器。

creators.name: Tarun Nayar
creators.role: Musician and former biologist; creator of the Modern Biology project
creators.bio: Canadian electronic musician who performs and records with plants and mushrooms wired to synthesizers under the name Modern Biology.
creators.why: Brought plant and fungal biodata music to a very large online audience.
creators.role_zh: 音乐人、前生物学研究者；Modern Biology 项目创作者
creators.bio_zh: 加拿大电子音乐人，以 Modern Biology 之名，把植物和蘑菇接入合成器进行演出和录音。
creators.why_zh: 让植物与真菌的生物数据音乐触及了非常庞大的网络观众。

creators.name: Studio diip
creators.role: Design studio for computer vision and interactive installations
creators.bio: Dutch studio that builds interactive projects based on computer vision.
creators.why: Its Fish on Wheels showed that a pet fish can drive a vehicle with off-the-shelf vision software.
creators.role_zh: 计算机视觉与互动装置设计工作室
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰工作室，制作基于计算机视觉的互动项目。
creators.why_zh: 他们的 Fish on Wheels 说明：用现成的视觉软件，宠物鱼就能驾驶车辆。

creators.name: Susana Soares
creators.role: Designer; senior lecturer, London South Bank University
creators.bio: Portuguese designer whose speculative projects explore how other species' senses could be used in health and everyday life.
creators.why: Bee's proposes trained bees as a diagnostic interface, a clear case of an organism as sensor.
creators.role_zh: 设计师；伦敦南岸大学高级讲师
creators.bio_zh: 葡萄牙设计师，她的思辨设计项目探索如何把其他物种的感官用于健康与日常生活。
creators.why_zh: Bee's 提出用训练过的蜜蜂做诊断界面，是「生物即传感器」的典型案例。

works.title: The Physarum Experiments
works.description: An ongoing series of numbered time-lapse studies in which slime mould solves mazes, fuses with other colonies, starves and forages on designed food landscapes.
works.description_zh: 一个持续进行的编号影像研究系列：延时摄影记录黏菌走迷宫、与其他菌落融合、在饥饿中扩散，以及在设计好的食物地形上觅食。
works.idea_en: Set up simple spatial problems and let a brainless organism draw its own solution over time.
works.idea_zh: 设置简单的空间问题，让一个没有大脑的生物用时间画出自己的答案。
works.method: Physarum polycephalum is cultured on agar with oat flakes as attractants and light or salt as repellents, and filmed with time-lapse photography and microscopy.
works.method_zh: 在琼脂上培养多头绒泡菌，用燕麦片作为吸引物、光或盐作为排斥物，并用延时摄影和显微拍摄记录。

works.title: Being Slime Mould
works.description: A participatory game in which groups of people follow a few rules taken from slime mould behaviour and try to find food and move as one body without a leader.
works.description_zh: 一个参与式游戏：一群人遵循从黏菌行为中提炼的几条规则，在没有领导者的情况下寻找“食物”并像一个身体一样移动。
works.idea_en: Borrow the rules of a single-celled organism to let people feel how collective decisions emerge.
works.idea_zh: 借用单细胞生物的规则，让人亲身体会集体决策是如何涌现的。
works.method: Participants enact Physarum behaviours such as oscillation, pulsing contact and retreat from repellents, informed by the artist's lab work with the organism; devised with Daniel Grushkin.
works.method_zh: 参与者根据艺术家在实验室中对多头绒泡菌的观察，模仿振荡、脉动接触和避开排斥物等行为；与 Daniel Grushkin 共同设计。

works.title: The Foragers
works.description: An experimental film made with about a thousand pavement ants, whose foraging trails across a new territory are tracked and turned into images.
works.description_zh: 一部与约一千只路面蚂蚁合作的实验影片：追踪它们在新领地上的觅食路径，并把轨迹转化为图像。
works.idea_en: Use a colony's chemical communication as an image-making system.
works.idea_zh: 把蚁群的化学通讯当作一种成像系统。
works.method: Time-lapse photography and image processing trace the pheromone trails of Tetramorium tsushimae ants as they search for food; made during a residency with The Swarm Lab.
works.method_zh: 用延时摄影和图像处理追踪路面蚂蚁（Tetramorium tsushimae）觅食时留下的信息素路径；在 The Swarm Lab 驻留期间完成。

works.title: Resilient Topographies #1: the peninsula of Paljassaare
works.description: A film in which slime mould grows across a model of the Paljassaare peninsula in Tallinn, mapping routes and resources on a contested post-industrial landscape.
works.description_zh: 一部影片：黏菌在塔林 Paljassaare 半岛的地形模型上生长，在这片有争议的后工业景观上绘出路径与资源分布。
works.idea_en: Let a living organism read a city site and propose its own network.
works.idea_zh: 让一个活的生物去“阅读”一块城市场地，并提出它自己的网络。
works.method: Physarum polycephalum was grown on an agar map of the peninsula with food sources at chosen locations and filmed in time-lapse, for the Tallinn Architecture Biennale 2017.
works.method_zh: 在半岛形状的琼脂地图上，于选定位置放置食物，培养多头绒泡菌并延时拍摄；为 2017 年塔林建筑双年展创作。

works.title: Swarm | Cell | City
works.description: A two-day workshop in Berlin where participants walked the city with GPS trackers following slime mould rules, while real slime mould grew on maps of the same area.
works.description_zh: 在柏林举行的两天工作坊：参与者带着 GPS 按黏菌规则在城市中行走，同时真实的黏菌在同一区域的地图上生长。
works.idea_en: Compare how people and a slime mould explore the same city, and let each trace inform the other.
works.idea_zh: 比较人和黏菌如何探索同一座城市，让两种轨迹互相参照。
works.method: Physarum polycephalum cultures on city maps were compared with participants' GPS walking traces; made with the artist duo plan b (Sophia New and Daniel Belasco Rogers) at Art Laboratory Berlin.
works.method_zh: 把城市地图上的多头绒泡菌培养物与参与者的 GPS 行走轨迹作对比；与艺术家组合 plan b（Sophia New、Daniel Belasco Rogers）在 Art Laboratory Berlin 合作完成。

works.title: bodymetries
works.description: An interactive table where visitors lay their arms down, a camera scans the skin, and a slime mould simulation grows networks between their moles and marks.
works.description_zh: 一张互动桌：观众把手臂放上去，摄像头扫描皮肤，黏菌模拟程序在痣和斑点之间长出网络。
works.idea_en: Map the human body with the spatial logic of a slime mould.
works.idea_zh: 用黏菌的空间逻辑来测绘人体。
works.method: Lab experiments with living Physarum polycephalum informed a multi-user Processing simulation of its network growth, projected onto visitors' arms via camera tracking and OSC.
works.method_zh: 以活体多头绒泡菌的实验室实验为依据，用 Processing 编写多用户网络生长模拟，通过摄像头追踪和 OSC 投影到观众手臂上。

works.title: Chroma + Phy
works.description: A speculative living wearable that would combine slime mould protoplasm with chameleon colour cells, so the garment changes colour with the wearer's mood.
works.description_zh: 一件思辨性的活体可穿戴装置：设想把黏菌原生质与变色龙的色素细胞结合，让衣物随穿戴者情绪变色。
works.idea_en: Imagine clothing made of living cells that signal the wearer's state to others.
works.idea_zh: 想象一种由活细胞构成的衣物，把穿戴者的状态显示给他人。
works.method: Prototype glassware with Physarum polycephalum, colour experiments and an HD film present the concept; the chromatophore hybrid is fictional.
works.method_zh: 用装有多头绒泡菌的玻璃器皿原型、颜色实验和高清影片呈现这一构想；与色素细胞的杂合体是虚构的。

works.title: Growing Geometries – tattooing mushrooms
works.description: The artist tattoos circles, squares and triangles into living mushrooms and records over a growth cycle how the fungus deforms the lines into new shapes.
works.description_zh: 艺术家把圆、方、三角形纹在活蘑菇上，并在一个生长周期内记录真菌如何把这些线条改造成新的形状。
works.idea_en: Use a growing organism as a slow image processor that rewrites a human drawing.
works.idea_zh: 把生长中的生物当作缓慢的图像处理器，让它改写人的绘图。
works.method: Geometric lines are tattooed into fungal fruiting bodies; a Raspberry Pi camera shoots time-lapse images that become an animation of the changing tattoos.
works.method_zh: 用纹身机在真菌子实体上刺入几何线条；树莓派相机拍摄延时照片，制成纹身图形变化的动画。

works.title: Sound for Fungi. Homage to Indeterminacy
works.description: An interactive video where a visitor's hand acts as a sound frequency that changes simulated hyphae growth in real time, based on an experiment in which the artist played tones to forest fungi.
works.description_zh: 一件互动影像：观众的手充当一个声音频率，实时改变模拟菌丝的生长；它源自艺术家向森林真菌播放声音的实验。
works.idea_en: Ask how fungi perceive sound, then let people play that role.
works.idea_zh: 先问真菌如何感知声音，再让人来扮演这个声音。
works.method: Mycelia collected near Berlin grew in sound-insulated boxes under sine tones and mostly grew faster and denser; the installation simulates this in openFrameworks with Leap Motion hand tracking.
works.method_zh: 从柏林附近采集的菌丝在隔音箱中接受正弦波声音刺激，多数长得更快更密；装置用 openFrameworks 和 Leap Motion 手势追踪模拟这一过程。
keywords: Prix Ars Electronica Artificial Intelligence & Life Art 2021

works.title: inside an inside forest
works.description: A room lined with tree bark and a hunting seat, where speaker cones double as bioreactors: sine waves keep liquid Reishi cultures moving while forming cymatic patterns.
works.description_zh: 一间铺满树皮、摆着狩猎高台的房间，扬声器同时充当生物反应器：正弦波让液体中的灵芝培养物保持流动，并在液面形成声纹图案。
works.idea_en: Let sound be both the artwork and the life support of the organism inside it.
works.idea_zh: 让声音既是作品本身，又是里面生物的生命维持系统。
works.method: Ganoderma (Reishi) mycelium grows in submerged culture inside speaker chassis, stirred and oxygenated by a 4-channel sine-wave composition.
works.method_zh: 灵芝菌丝在扬声器腔体内进行液体深层培养，由四声道正弦波作品搅动并供氧。

works.title: ooze
works.description: A double 4K projection of laser-scanned forests and server farms whose motion and sound are driven by sensor data from living microalgae bioreactors that visitors can light with their phones.
works.description_zh: 双 4K 投影展示激光扫描的森林和服务器机房，画面运动和声音由活体微藻生物反应器的传感数据驱动，观众可以用手机灯光照射藻类。
works.idea_en: Use a living culture as an analogue random generator that brings real unpredictability into a digital work.
works.idea_zh: 把活的培养物当作模拟随机数发生器，为数字作品带来真正的不可预测性。
works.method: Sensors monitor growth and metabolism of microalgae in custom bioreactors and stream parameters to point-cloud visuals and sound; made with Ivan Taranin and TU Berlin Bioprocess Engineering.
works.method_zh: 传感器监测定制生物反应器中微藻的生长与代谢，并把参数实时传给点云影像和声音；与 Ivan Taranin 及柏林工业大学生物过程工程系合作。

works.title: Hylē
works.description: A bio-cybernetic installation in which visitors' breath feeds CO2 to an algae sculpture, whose sensor signals alter projected point clouds, while the projection light in turn feeds the algae.
works.description_zh: 一件生物控制论装置：观众呼出的二氧化碳供给藻类雕塑，藻类的传感信号改变投影中的点云，而投影光又反过来喂养藻类。
works.idea_en: Close a loop of breathing between a human, algae and a machine.
works.idea_zh: 在人、藻类和机器之间建立一个呼吸循环。
works.method: Custom bioreactors with CO2 and TDS sensors read by Raspberry Pis stream algae data to two 4K point-cloud projections and sound; made with Ivan Taranin.
works.method_zh: 定制生物反应器配有二氧化碳和 TDS 传感器，由树莓派读取藻类数据并驱动两路 4K 点云投影和声音；与 Ivan Taranin 合作。

works.title: Biocomputer Rhythms
works.description: A piece for piano with electromagnets and percussion, composed and performed with PhyBox, a stand-alone biocomputer built from slime mould memristors.
works.description_zh: 一首为带电磁装置的钢琴和打击乐而作的作品，用由黏菌忆阻器构成的独立生物计算机 PhyBox 来作曲和演奏。
works.idea_en: Grow the electronic components of a music machine instead of manufacturing them.
works.idea_zh: 音乐机器的电子元件可以“长出来”，而不是制造出来。
works.method: Physarum polycephalum grown in 3D-printed barrels with electrodes acts as biomemristors in PhyBox, which generates rhythmic responses that drive electromagnets vibrating piano strings and percussion.
works.method_zh: 多头绒泡菌生长在带电极的 3D 打印小筒中，作为 PhyBox 里的生物忆阻器；PhyBox 生成的节奏回应驱动电磁铁振动钢琴琴弦和打击乐器。
keywords: Prix Ars Electronica Artificial Intelligence & Life Art 2019

works.title: Jurema Action Plant
works.description: A robotic structure carrying a sensitive plant (Mimosa pudica) that reads the plant's electrical response to touch and moves it away from the person touching it.
works.description_zh: 一个载着含羞草的机器人结构：它读取植物被触碰时的电信号，并带着植物避开触碰它的人。
works.idea_en: Give a plant the ability to flee by wiring its own signals to wheels.
works.idea_zh: 把植物自身的电信号接到轮子上，让它获得逃离的能力。
works.method: Electrodes on the branches pick up action potentials, which an amplifier turns into triggers for the robot's motors; developed at V2_ Lab with Fytagoras and Leiden University biologists.
works.method_zh: 枝条上的电极采集动作电位，经放大器转换为驱动机器人电机的信号；在 V2_ Lab 与 Fytagoras 和莱顿大学生物学家合作开发。

works.title: e-SEED
works.description: A seed encased in a bio-solar cell that uses electricity from photosynthetic components to stimulate its own growth, proposed as a tool to revive barren land.
works.description_zh: 一颗被包裹在生物太阳能电池中的种子，利用光合元件产生的电能刺激自身生长，被设想为复苏荒地的工具。
works.idea_en: Package a seed with its own biological power supply.
works.idea_zh: 给种子配上它自己的生物电源。
works.method: A bio-solar cell likely built from photosynthetic proteins of bacteria generates current that is applied to the seed; developed with VU Amsterdam biophysics and ESA Space Garden.
works.method_zh: 生物太阳能电池（很可能由细菌的光合蛋白构成）产生电流并施加给种子；与阿姆斯特丹自由大学生物物理系及欧洲航天局 Space Garden 合作开发。

works.title: C-DER
works.description: A swarm of autonomous robots that exchange gases with their surroundings through micro-algae photosynthesis while dispersing seeds to restore damaged land.
works.description_zh: 一群自主机器人，通过微藻光合作用与周围环境交换气体，同时播撒种子以修复受损土地。
works.idea_en: Design robots whose main job is to breathe and plant for an ecosystem.
works.idea_zh: 设计一种以“呼吸”和“播种”为主要工作的生态机器人。
works.method: Each unit carries micro-algae cultures for photosynthetic gas exchange and a seeding mechanism; developed with VU Amsterdam biophysics, Ghent University CMET, CEFET/RJ and ESA Space Garden.
works.method_zh: 每个单元携带用于光合气体交换的微藻培养物和播种装置；与阿姆斯特丹自由大学生物物理系、根特大学 CMET、CEFET/RJ 和欧洲航天局 Space Garden 合作开发。

works.title: Prototype for a New BioMachine
works.description: A follow-up to Jurema Action Plant in which a robotic structure moves when visitors touch the leaves of the plant it carries.
works.description_zh: 《Jurema Action Plant》的延续：当观众触碰机器人所载植物的叶子时，机器人结构随之移动。
works.idea_en: Move toward self-sustaining machines where plant signals and electronics form one body.
works.idea_zh: 朝向一种自我维持的机器：植物信号和电子元件构成同一个身体。
works.method: Bioelectric data from the plant are processed by electronic circuits that drive the robot's motors; exhibited at the Verbeke Foundation.
works.method_zh: 植物的生物电数据经电子电路处理后驱动机器人电机；展于 Verbeke Foundation。

works.title: Ecoshroom
works.description: A glass pavilion of plants colonised by mycorrhizal fungi, where a machine learning system reads their bioelectric signals and adjusts light, humidity and air to keep them well, and sonifies their state.
works.description_zh: 一座玻璃亭，里面的植物与菌根真菌共生；机器学习系统读取它们的生物电信号，调节光照、湿度和空气以维持其健康，并把它们的状态转化为声音。
works.idea_en: Let plants and fungi steer the climate of a building through their own signals.
works.idea_zh: 让植物和真菌通过自身信号来调节建筑内的气候。
works.method: Electrodes record signals from plants and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi alongside light, temperature, humidity, CO2 and soil moisture; a custom model learns to control the environment; with Toby Kiers's lab and others.
works.method_zh: 电极记录植物和丛枝菌根真菌的信号，同时采集光照、温度、湿度、二氧化碳和土壤湿度；定制模型学习如何控制环境；与 Toby Kiers 实验室等合作。

works.title: Mycophone_emergence
works.description: A biohacked music box: winding it sends a signal through a mycelium culture that changes the sound, and petting the hairy mycelium makes its voice change as if it purrs.
works.description_zh: 一个被“生物黑客”改造的音乐盒：上紧发条后，信号穿过菌丝培养物并改变声音；抚摸毛茸茸的菌丝，它的声音会变，像在打呼噜。
works.idea_en: Make a living network part of a sound instrument that needs care to keep playing.
works.idea_zh: 让一个活的网络成为乐器的一部分，而这件乐器需要照料才能继续演奏。
works.method: A signal from the wound music box passes through a growing mycelium whose conductivity, touch and proximity modulate the sound; made with Mirjan Švagelj and Anil Podgornik.
works.method_zh: 发条音乐盒产生的信号穿过生长中的菌丝，菌丝的导电性以及触摸和靠近都会调制声音；与 Mirjan Švagelj 和 Anil Podgornik 合作。

works.title: Mycophone_unison
works.description: A sound map in which a visitor presses a fingerprint to send a signal through cultures of the three authors' microbiomes, which modulate it into a single sound of unison.
works.description_zh: 一张声音地图：观众按下指纹，把信号送入三位作者的微生物组培养物，由它们调制成一个“齐奏”的声音。
works.idea_en: Hear a human body as many organisms acting together for a moment.
works.idea_zh: 把人的身体听成许多生物在某一刻共同发声。
works.method: Signals are routed through living cultures of fungi and microbes taken from the authors' bodies, whose electrical properties likely alter the sound; made with Mirjan Švagelj and Anil Podgornik, produced by KIBLA.
works.method_zh: 信号被送入取自作者身体的真菌和微生物活体培养物，它们的电学特性很可能改变了声音；与 Mirjan Švagelj 和 Anil Podgornik 合作，由 KIBLA 制作。

works.title: Symbiome – Economy of Symbiosis
works.description: A hydroponic chamber of red clover and nitrogen-fixing bacteria whose nutrient exchange sets the rhythm of water drops; the ripples are turned into real-time sound.
works.description_zh: 一个水培舱，里面是红三叶草和固氮细菌；它们之间的养分交换决定水滴的节奏，涟漪被实时转化为声音。
works.idea_en: Make a symbiotic negotiation audible, and let visitors' breath enter it.
works.idea_zh: 让共生关系中的“谈判”被听见，并让观众的呼吸也加入进来。
works.method: Indirect measurements of the Trifolium pratense–Rhizobium exchange, likely pH of the hydroponic solution, control a dripper; ripples are captured and phase-modulated into sound, and visitors' exhaled CO2 affects the plant.
works.method_zh: 对红三叶草与根瘤菌之间交换的间接测量（很可能是水培液的 pH）控制滴水器；水面涟漪被采集并经相位调制转化为声音，观众呼出的二氧化碳也会影响植物。

works.title: Earthlink
works.description: A system of installations about breathing with the planet: visitors inhale soil bacteria in rhythm with resuscitator bags, exhale their microbiome into artificial lungs, and meet a clover–bacteria symbiosis.
works.description_zh: 一组关于与地球共同呼吸的装置：观众随着复苏气囊的节奏吸入土壤细菌，把自己的微生物组呼入人造肺中，并面对三叶草与细菌的共生系统。
works.idea_en: Show breathing as an exchange with microbes that technology can mediate and control.
works.idea_zh: 把呼吸呈现为一种与微生物的交换，而这种交换可以被技术中介和控制。
works.method: Inspiration delivers Mycobacterium vaccae aerosol paced by resuscitator bags; Expiration collects exhaled microbes in external lungs washed with cypress extract; Symbiome links Trifolium pratense and Rhizobium.
works.method_zh: 《Inspiration》以复苏气囊控制节奏输送母牛分枝杆菌（Mycobacterium vaccae）气溶胶；《Expiration》把呼出的微生物收集到外置“肺”中并用柏树提取液冲洗；《Symbiome》连接红三叶草与根瘤菌。

works.title: Gut-Machine Poetry
works.description: A homebrew computer fuelled by a kombucha ferment, whose bacterial and yeast activity acts as a random number generator for producing a new kind of language.
works.description_zh: 一台自制电脑，以康普茶发酵物为“燃料”，其中细菌和酵母的活动充当随机数发生器，用来生成一种新的语言。
works.idea_en: Let a gut-like microbial culture write, so language comes from digestion rather than a mind.
works.idea_zh: 让一个类似肠道的微生物群落来“写作”，语言来自消化而不是头脑。
works.method: Fluctuations in a SCOBY kombucha culture, likely read by sensors, seed a text-generating program; commissioned by Kiasma, with Vincent de Belleval and Johanna Lundberg.
works.method_zh: 康普茶菌膜（SCOBY）培养物中的波动（很可能由传感器读取）作为文本生成程序的随机种子；由 Kiasma 委托，与 Vincent de Belleval 和 Johanna Lundberg 合作。

works.title: Minakata Mandala
works.description: Slime mould grows through a labyrinth shaped after the mandala drawn by the naturalist Kumagusu Minakata, finding its own route between oat flakes.
works.description_zh: 黏菌在一座按博物学家南方熊楠所绘曼陀罗塑造的迷宫中生长，在燕麦片之间找出自己的路线。
works.idea_en: Hand a diagram of the world to a decentralised organism and watch it reorganise it.
works.idea_zh: 把一张世界图式交给一个去中心化的生物，看它如何重新组织它。
works.method: Physarum polycephalum on agar navigates a mandala-shaped maze baited with oat flakes; part of a series of organisational labyrinths.
works.method_zh: 多头绒泡菌在琼脂上穿行于一个以燕麦片为诱饵的曼陀罗形迷宫；属于“组织迷宫”系列。

works.title: Vermi-Cell
works.description: A living sculpture of soil, metals, worms and food waste whose electricity powers a saxophone voice and pulsing lights.
works.description_zh: 一件由土壤、金属、蚯蚓和厨余构成的活体雕塑，它产生的电能驱动萨克斯风声音和闪烁的灯光。
works.idea_en: Let a compost ecosystem be the battery and the voice of an artwork.
works.idea_zh: 让一个堆肥生态系统同时成为作品的电池和声音。
works.method: Metal electrodes in active vermicompost form an earth battery, likely a soil microbial fuel cell, whose output drives sound and LEDs.
works.method_zh: 活跃蚯蚓堆肥中的金属电极构成“土壤电池”（很可能是土壤微生物燃料电池），其输出驱动声音和 LED。

works.title: Vermi-Sibyl
works.description: A compost oracle on the roof of the Swiss Institute in New York, powered by an earth battery and summoned in a live performance with a saxophonist and voice actors.
works.description_zh: 纽约瑞士学院屋顶上的一座“堆肥神谕”，由土壤电池供电，并在一场有萨克斯手和配音演员参与的现场表演中被“召唤”。
works.idea_en: Treat a compost heap as a speaking, energy-giving oracle.
works.idea_zh: 把一堆堆肥当作会说话、能供能的神谕。
works.method: Worms and soil microbes in a compost bin generate current through an earth battery, likely a soil microbial fuel cell, that powers the oracle's voice; performed as Midden (LIVE) for Performa Biennial.
works.method_zh: 堆肥箱中的蚯蚓和土壤微生物通过土壤电池（很可能是土壤微生物燃料电池）产生电流，为神谕的声音供电；以《Midden (LIVE)》为题在 Performa 双年展上演出。

works.title: PL'AI
works.description: Over several months an AI robot with 36 wires plays with cucumber plants at their own pace, moving coloured balls toward them while the tendrils grab and reshape the wires into a trellis.
works.description_zh: 在数月时间里，一个带有 36 根吊线的 AI 机器人以黄瓜的速度与它们“玩耍”，把彩球移向植物，而卷须抓住吊线并把它们改造成支架。
works.idea_en: Imagine play, not work, as the basis of a relationship between plants and machines.
works.idea_zh: 把“玩耍”而非“劳动”当作植物与机器关系的基础。
works.method: A laser scanner images the cucumbers, a neural network decides how to move 36 individually controlled strings at about 1 cm per hour, and tendril growth feeds back into the model.
works.method_zh: 激光扫描仪获取黄瓜图像，神经网络决定如何以约每小时 1 厘米的速度移动 36 根独立控制的吊线，卷须的生长再反馈回模型。
keywords: Prix Ars Electronica Artificial Intelligence & Life Art 2021

works.title: Institute for Inconspicuous Languages: Reading Lips
works.description: An attempt to build a sign language with a ficus tree by reading the opening and closing of its leaf stomata and answering with codes of light.
works.description_zh: 尝试与一棵榕树建立手语：读取叶片气孔的开合，并用光的编码作出回应。
works.idea_en: Look for a shared code with a plant through the body part it already uses to regulate itself.
works.idea_zh: 通过植物本来就用来自我调节的器官，寻找与它共享的编码。
works.method: Microscope cameras and computer vision track stomata on Ficus benjamina leaves, and light signals are given as Pavlovian conditioning cues; built with Bart Peeters, Klara Nosan and Tim Oblak.
works.method_zh: 显微摄像头和计算机视觉追踪垂叶榕叶片上的气孔，用光信号作为巴甫洛夫式条件反射提示；与 Bart Peeters、Klara Nosan 和 Tim Oblak 合作完成。

works.title: Vegetariat: Work Zero
works.description: Popular potted office plants are wired to smart watches that report their activity to fitness apps, feeding plant data into the prediction algorithms of platform companies.
works.description_zh: 流行的室内盆栽被连接到智能手表上，手表把它们的“活动”报告给健身应用，让植物数据流入平台公司的预测算法。
works.idea_en: Let plants perform as data workers to confuse and critique surveillance capitalism.
works.idea_zh: 让植物充当数据劳工，以扰乱和批判监控资本主义。
works.method: An electro-mechanical interface likely translates plant movement or bioelectric changes into motion that smart watches register as activity; interface by Gregor Krpič, realised by Scenart.
works.method_zh: 机电接口很可能把植物的运动或生物电变化转化为机械运动，被智能手表记录为“活动量”；接口由 Gregor Krpič 开发，Scenart 制作。

works.title: Miserable Machines
works.description: Mussels are strapped into an electro-stimulation apparatus that makes them contract every twenty minutes, scratching a design into a slowly rising vase until they die.
works.description_zh: 贻贝被固定在电刺激装置中，每二十分钟收缩一次，在一只缓慢上升的花瓶上刻出图案，直至死去。
works.idea_en: Show the ethical cost of plugging living bodies into production machines.
works.idea_zh: 揭示把活体接入生产机器的伦理代价。
works.method: Electrical stimulation triggers muscle contractions of mussels whose shells scratch a rotating cylinder that moves about 20 cm in six hours; designed with Miha Turšič, produced by MU Eindhoven.
works.method_zh: 电刺激引发贻贝肌肉收缩，贝壳在旋转圆柱上划出痕迹，圆柱六小时内上升约 20 厘米；与 Miha Turšič 共同设计，由埃因霍温 MU 制作。

works.title: Deep Swamp
works.description: Three wetland tanks are each tended by an AI agent that adjusts light, water flow, fog and nutrients to reach its goal: a natural wetland, a work of art, or attention.
works.description_zh: 三个湿地水箱各由一个 AI 代理照管，它们调节光照、水流、雾气和养分，分别追求“自然的湿地”“一件艺术品”或“获得关注”。
works.idea_en: Ask what happens when software with narrow goals manages living ecosystems.
works.idea_zh: 追问当目标狭隘的软件管理活的生态系统时会发生什么。
works.method: Each agent photographs its tank, compares images against goals learned by deep learning from tagged online image collections, and tries new combinations of misters, pumps and lights.
works.method_zh: 每个代理拍摄自己的水箱，把照片与深度学习从带标签的在线图库中学到的目标相比较，再尝试新的雾化器、水泵和灯光组合。

works.title: Coin-Operated Wetland
works.description: A working laundromat whose washing machines run on water cleaned by a constructed wetland, so each wash depends on the health of the plants.
works.description_zh: 一个真正运转的自助洗衣房，洗衣机使用经人工湿地净化后的水，因此每一次洗衣都取决于植物的健康状况。
works.idea_en: Connect an everyday action directly to an ecosystem so that care becomes part of use.
works.idea_zh: 把日常行为直接接到一个生态系统上，让照料成为使用的一部分。
works.method: Greywater from commercial washers is pumped through gravel beds planted with wetland species, where plants and root-zone microbes treat it for reuse.
works.method_zh: 商用洗衣机排出的灰水被泵入种有湿地植物的砾石床，由植物及根区微生物处理后循环使用。

works.title: Why Not Hand Over a "Shelter" to Hermit Crabs?
works.description: Hermit crabs are offered clear 3D-printed shells topped with miniature city skylines, and choose whether to move in.
works.description_zh: 艺术家为寄居蟹提供顶部带有微缩城市天际线的透明 3D 打印贝壳，由它们自己决定是否搬进去。
works.idea_en: Design a home for another species and let the animal decide whether it fits.
works.idea_zh: 为另一个物种设计住所，并让动物自己决定是否合适。
works.method: CT scans of abandoned shells give the interior geometry; resin shells with city forms are 3D-printed and placed in the crabs' tank.
works.method_zh: 用 CT 扫描被遗弃贝壳得到内部结构，再 3D 打印带有城市造型的树脂贝壳并放入寄居蟹的水箱。

works.title: girl, girl, girl . . .
works.description: Bagworm larvae are given scraps of women's clothing and build their protective cases from them, producing tiny garments made by insects.
works.description_zh: 艺术家给蓑蛾幼虫提供女性衣物的碎布，幼虫用它们搭建自己的巢筒，做出由昆虫“缝制”的小衣服。
works.idea_en: Let an insect's building behaviour become fashion design.
works.idea_zh: 让昆虫的筑巢行为变成时装设计。
works.method: Bagworm larvae spin silk to bind fabric scraps into cases, a traditional Japanese children's pastime done with paper strips.
works.method_zh: 蓑蛾幼虫吐丝把碎布粘合成巢筒；日本儿童传统上用彩纸条玩这个游戏。

works.title: How to Carve a Sculpture
works.description: Beavers in zoos gnaw wooden blocks, and the artist scans the results and has them enlarged and recarved as sculptures, with the sound of chewing.
works.description_zh: 动物园里的河狸啃咬木块，艺术家把啃出的形状扫描后放大并重新雕刻成雕塑，配以啃咬的声音。
works.idea_en: Question authorship by treating an animal's gnawing as sculpture.
works.idea_zh: 把动物的啃咬当作雕塑，以此质疑作者身份。
works.method: Wood gnawed by beavers at several Japanese zoos is 3D-scanned and machine-carved at larger scale in wood, shown with recordings and video.
works.method_zh: 把日本多家动物园里河狸啃过的木头进行 3D 扫描，再用机器以更大尺寸在木材上雕刻，并配以录音和影像展出。

works.title: Phonofolium
works.description: A living shrub that sings when visitors stroke or approach it, each touch producing a different sound character.
works.description_zh: 一株活的灌木，观众抚摸或靠近它时会“唱歌”，每次触碰都产生不同的声音。
works.idea_en: Turn a plant into a sensor of human touch and give it a voice.
works.idea_zh: 把植物变成感知人类触摸的传感器，并赋予它声音。
works.method: The plant and the visitor's body form a capacitive circuit that detects electrostatic changes from touch and proximity, mapped to generative sound.
works.method_zh: 植物与观众的身体构成电容回路，检测触摸和靠近引起的静电变化，并映射为生成声音。

works.title: Domestic Plant
works.description: A potted plant on a small robot that moves and makes sounds when people touch it, behaving like a wild animal kept on a leash.
works.description_zh: 一盆放在小型机器人上的植物，人触碰它时它会移动并发出声音，像一只被拴住的野生动物。
works.idea_en: Give a plant animal-like mobility and ask what domestication means for it.
works.idea_zh: 赋予植物类似动物的移动能力，并追问“驯化”对它意味着什么。
works.method: Capacitive sensing through the plant detects touch and triggers sound and the movement of a Magabot mobile robot base.
works.method_zh: 通过植物的电容感应检测触摸，触发声音和 Magabot 移动机器人底座的运动。

works.title: Phytopoiesis
works.description: A living plant that reacts to touch with sound and sends prompts to a local image generator, producing ever-changing hybrids of plant and human bodies on a facing screen.
works.description_zh: 一株活植物对触摸作出声音回应，并向本地图像生成模型发送提示词，在对面的屏幕上生成不断变化的植物与人体混合图像。
works.idea_en: Let a plant author the prompts of a generative AI.
works.idea_zh: 让植物成为生成式 AI 提示词的作者。
works.method: Electrostatic touch sensing through the plant triggers sound and prompt generation for Stable Diffusion running offline on a local computer.
works.method_zh: 通过植物进行静电触摸感应，触发声音并为离线运行在本地电脑上的 Stable Diffusion 生成提示词。

works.title: The Surface Dynamics of Adhesion
works.description: Living Candida albicans grows on agar made with the artist's blood in acrylic boxes, forming a wallpaper pattern that the yeast slowly escapes during the exhibition.
works.description_zh: 活的白色念珠菌在用艺术家血液制成的琼脂上生长，封装在亚克力盒中，形成壁纸图案，而酵母在展期中慢慢“逃出”图案。
works.idea_en: Stage a human-microbe relationship as a living ornament that refuses to stay in line.
works.idea_zh: 把人与微生物的关系呈现为一种不肯守规矩的活体装饰。
works.method: C. albicans is inoculated on blood agar containing the artist's blood in a pattern adapted from Charles Philippe Robin's 1853 drawing of the organism.
works.method_zh: 按照 Charles Philippe Robin 1853 年绘制的该生物图样，把白色念珠菌接种在含有艺术家血液的血琼脂上。

works.title: Organic Cinema
works.description: A live cinema in which the electrical responses of common plants decide the order and variation of projected images and sound.
works.description_zh: 一部“现场电影”：普通植物的电信号反应决定投影画面和声音的顺序与变化。
works.idea_en: Make plants the actors and editors of a film.
works.idea_zh: 让植物成为一部电影的演员和剪辑师。
works.method: Sensors read action and variation potentials from plants in real time, and an algorithm maps them to sequences of pre-made imagery and sound; by World Wilder Lab.
works.method_zh: 传感器实时读取植物的动作电位和变异电位，算法把它们映射为预先制作的影像和声音序列；World Wilder Lab 作品。

works.title: Plandscapes
works.description: A chosen plant streams its internal biosignals into algorithms that draw generative images, and also decides which drawings are printed and shown.
works.description_zh: 一株被选中的植物把体内的生物信号传给算法生成图画，并决定哪些图画被打印展出。
works.idea_en: Treat a plant as the artist with its own style.
works.idea_zh: 把植物当作拥有自己风格的艺术家。
works.method: The PlanEt device designed by World Wilder Lab acquires biodata from inside the plant (first a Fatsia japonica) and feeds custom drawing algorithms and a printer.
works.method_zh: World Wilder Lab 设计的 PlanEt 设备从植物内部（首件作品是八角金盘）采集生物数据，输入定制绘图算法和打印机。

works.title: (de)Compositions
works.description: A soil monolith in which earthworms mix fertile and depleted soil over weeks, while sensors turn their activity and the changing moisture into a slowly shifting spatial sound piece.
works.description_zh: 一块土壤“巨石”，蚯蚓在数周内把肥沃与贫瘠的土壤混合；传感器把它们的活动和变化的湿度转化为缓慢变化的空间声音作品。
works.idea_en: Pair living biosensors with digital sensors so data never loses its source.
works.idea_zh: 把活的生物传感器与数字传感器配对，让数据不脱离它的来源。
works.method: Moisture sensors and piezo sensors track soil conditions and worm activity in a layered container, driving at least four speakers and proximity-triggered lights; with GROW Observatory, commissioned by STARTS.
works.method_zh: 湿度传感器和压电传感器追踪分层容器中的土壤状况与蚯蚓活动，驱动至少四个扬声器和感应灯光；与 GROW Observatory 合作，由 STARTS 委托。

works.title: Sonic Garden
works.description: An interactive garden at Sonos Studio in Los Angeles where visitors touch plants and hear generative music made from the plants' bioelectric signals.
works.description_zh: 洛杉矶 Sonos Studio 的一座互动花园，观众触摸植物，就能听到由植物生物电信号生成的音乐。
works.idea_en: Turn living plants into a public instrument through aesthetic sonification.
works.idea_zh: 通过审美化声音化，把活植物变成一件公共乐器。
works.method: Electrodes on leaves pick up bioelectric emissions, which generative software, likely written in SuperCollider, turns into sound played through a Sonos system.
works.method_zh: 叶片上的电极采集生物电信号，由生成软件（很可能用 SuperCollider 编写）转化为声音，并通过 Sonos 系统播放。

works.title: Pulsu(m) Plantae
works.description: A sound prosthesis reads the bioelectric activity of living plants and turns it into synthesised sound, so visitors can hear specimens respond over time.
works.description_zh: 一个“声音义肢”读取活体植物的生物电活动，并把它转化为合成声音，观众可以听到不同植株随时间的反应。
works.idea_en: Give plants an audible voice with a biofeedback prosthesis, and compare the patterns across species.
works.idea_zh: 用生物反馈式的“义肢”给植物一个能被听见的声音，并比较不同物种的模式。
works.method: Electrodes on leaves and stems pick up micro-voltage changes that drive a sound synthesis process; developed with UNAM botanist Juan Carlos González.
works.method_zh: 贴在叶片和茎上的电极采集微电压变化，用来驱动声音合成；与墨西哥国立自治大学植物学家 Juan Carlos González 合作开发。

works.title: Bio-Box
works.description: A live-performance interface that uses the electrical responses of mosses and algae to light, vibration and touch as analog control data for audio generators.
works.description_zh: 一个现场演出界面，把苔藓和藻类对光、振动和触碰的电反应当作模拟控制信号，实时驱动音频发生器。
works.idea_en: Let small plants play in a band: their gestures of micro-voltage become knobs on a synthesizer.
works.idea_zh: 让小型植物加入乐队：它们的微电压“手势”成了合成器上的旋钮。
works.method: Electrodes read micro-voltage from moss and algae cultures, amplified and mapped to control voltages of analog sound generators.
works.method_zh: 电极读取苔藓和藻类培养物的微电压，经放大后映射为模拟声音发生器的控制电压。

works.title: Energy Bending Lab
works.description: A set of custom modular synthesizers amplifies the micro-voltage of electrogenic bacteria and sonifies it in real time, then turns the sound into visible patterns through cymatics.
works.description_zh: 一套定制模块合成器放大产电细菌的微电压并实时转为声音，再通过音流学（cymatics）把声音变成可见的图案。
works.idea_en: Let bacterial voltage set the clock of the whole instrument, so the microbes pace the music.
works.idea_zh: 让细菌的电压成为整台乐器的时钟，由微生物来决定音乐的节奏。
works.method: Microbial fuel cells feed microvoltages into modular synthesizers that tune the system clock, and a cymatics plate converts the sound into patterns; built during ECAS residencies and at Bauhaus-Universität Weimar.
works.method_zh: 微生物燃料电池把微电压送入模块合成器并调节系统时钟，再由音流学振动板把声音变成图案；在 ECAS 驻留和魏玛包豪斯大学期间完成。

works.title: PhyChip / Phytracker
works.description: As artistic researchers in the EU PhyChip project on slime-mould computing, Interspecifics built Phytracker, a computer-vision tool that turns the growth and movement of Physarum into musical compositions.
works.description_zh: Interspecifics 作为艺术研究者参与了关于黏菌计算的欧盟 PhyChip 项目，开发了 Phytracker：一个把多头绒泡菌的生长与移动转化为音乐作品的计算机视觉工具。
works.idea_en: Read a slime mould's exploration as a score: its routing behaviour becomes the composition.
works.idea_zh: 把黏菌的探索路线当作乐谱：它的寻路行为就是作品。
works.method: A camera tracks Physarum polycephalum networks on agar and software maps their expansion to sound events; made at Bauhaus-Universität Weimar within the PhyChip consortium.
works.method_zh: 摄像头追踪琼脂上多头绒泡菌的网络，软件把它的扩展映射为声音事件；在魏玛包豪斯大学、PhyChip 项目框架内完成。

works.title: Geobacter Micropulse
works.description: Microbial fuel cells filled with New York seawater and sediment power light patterns whose fluctuations follow the bioelectric output of Geobacter communities, as a sketch of an encoded language.
works.description_zh: 装满纽约海水和沉积物的微生物燃料电池驱动灯光图案，其闪烁随地杆菌群落的生物电输出变化，像是一种编码语言的雏形。
works.idea_en: Treat the flicker of bacterial electricity as the first letters of an interspecies alphabet.
works.idea_zh: 把细菌电流的闪烁当作跨物种字母表的最初字母。
works.method: Anaerobic Geobacter consortia in sediment fuel cells release electrons whose voltage fluctuations are amplified to drive LED patterns.
works.method_zh: 沉积物燃料电池中的厌氧地杆菌群落释放电子，电压波动经放大后驱动 LED 图案。

works.title: Speculative Communications
works.description: A machine watches a microorganism culture, learns to recognise repeated coordinated actions in it and turns them into an auto-generative audiovisual score streamed live.
works.description_zh: 一台机器观察微生物培养物，学习识别其中重复出现的协同行为，并把它们转化为可在线直播的自生成视听乐谱。
works.idea_en: Build a SETI-style listening post for non-human intelligence right under the microscope.
works.idea_zh: 在显微镜下搭建一个类似 SETI 的非人类智能“监听站”。
works.method: A microscope camera and machine-learning system track behaviour patterns in a self-maintaining microbial culture (likely bacteria) and map them to musical and visual gestures; developed with support from FONCA, Laboratorio Arte Alameda, Medialab-Prado and DAAD.
works.method_zh: 显微摄像头和机器学习系统追踪一个可自我维护的微生物培养物（可能是细菌）的行为模式，并将其映射为音乐和视觉动作；得到 FONCA、Laboratorio Arte Alameda、Medialab-Prado 和 DAAD 支持。

works.title: Perejil Buscando al Sol (Parsley Looking for the Sun)
works.description: A small robot carrying a living parsley plant moves by itself to escape the shade of the city and find sunlight.
works.description_zh: 一个载着活欧芹的小机器人会自行移动，躲开城市阴影，寻找阳光。
works.idea_en: Give a plant wheels so it can act on its need for light.
works.idea_zh: 给植物装上轮子，让它能按自己对光的需求行动。
works.method: Photovoltaic cells, motors and a methacrylate body with soil and a living plant; the solar cells steer the vehicle toward brighter light (likely a simple light-seeking circuit).
works.method_zh: 由光伏电池、电机和装有土壤与活植物的有机玻璃外壳组成；太阳能电池驱动小车驶向更亮处（可能是简单的趋光电路）。

works.title: Plantas Nómadas (Nomadic Plants)
works.description: An autonomous walking robot sucks polluted river water into microbial fuel cells; the bacteria clean the water and produce electricity, and the cleaned water feeds plants growing on the robot's back.
works.description_zh: 一个会行走的自主机器人把受污染的河水吸进微生物燃料电池；细菌净化水并发电，净化后的水浇灌长在机器人背上的植物。
works.idea_en: Design a new 'species' whose metabolism is shared between robot, microbes and plants, and which repairs its habitat.
works.idea_zh: 设计一个新“物种”：它的新陈代谢由机器人、微生物和植物共同完成，并能修复所在的栖息地。
works.method: Microbial fuel cells with native bacteria biodegrade waste and charge batteries, photovoltaics drive locomotion, and the robot voices high pollution through sound; tested on the Lerma river.
works.method_zh: 内含本地细菌的微生物燃料电池降解污物并为电池充电，光伏板驱动行走，污染严重时机器人会发出声音；在莱尔马河畔测试。

works.title: Plantas Autofotosintéticas (Autophotosynthetic Plants)
works.description: Modular microbial fuel cells fed with city sewage produce electricity that lights a central aquarium, where plants, algae, protozoa and crustaceans live in balance; their waste is pumped back to the cells to restart the cycle.
works.description_zh: 以城市污水为燃料的模块化微生物燃料电池发电，点亮中央水缸；水缸里的植物、微藻、原生动物和甲壳类保持平衡，它们的排泄物再被泵回电池，重新开始循环。
works.idea_en: Close a loop in which sewage bacteria make the light that other organisms need to photosynthesise.
works.idea_zh: 形成一个闭环：污水中的细菌制造光，供其他生物进行光合作用。
works.method: Electrogenic bacteria in modular fuel cells release power as light pulses for aquatic plants, and an electronic monitoring network pumps water between the modules and the core ecosystem.
works.method_zh: 模块化燃料电池中的产电细菌把电能以光脉冲形式释放给水生植物，电子监测网络在各模块与核心生态系统之间泵送水体。

works.title: Voice of Nature
works.description: Sensors on the roots, leaves and branches of a living tree in Chengdu feed a display that grows a new tree ring every second, showing how the tree responds to pollution in real time.
works.description_zh: 成都一棵活树的根、叶和枝上装有传感器，数据驱动一块屏幕每秒生成一道新的年轮，实时呈现这棵树对污染的反应。
works.idea_en: Speed up a tree's own record-keeping, the growth ring, so people can read it on their timescale.
works.idea_zh: 把树木自带的记录方式——年轮——加速到人类的时间尺度，让人能读懂。
works.method: Twelve sensors measure CO2, temperature, moisture, photosynthesis and growth, and an algorithm renders the data as rings on a screen behind the tree; developed with TU Delft scientists.
works.method_zh: 12 个传感器测量二氧化碳、温度、湿度、光合作用和生长，算法把数据绘制成树后屏幕上的年轮；与代尔夫特理工大学的科学家合作。

works.title: Xylemia
works.description: A sculpture wrapped around a living tree shows the sap flowing through its xylem in real time, so visitors can compare the tree's circulation with their own.
works.description_zh: 一件缠绕在活树上的雕塑实时显示树木木质部中的液流，观众可以把树的“循环”与自己的血液循环相对照。
works.idea_en: Visualise a tree's internal flow as a pulse, so empathy starts from a shared physiology.
works.idea_zh: 把树的内部液流可视化为一种脉搏，从共同的生理节律出发引发共情。
works.method: Sap-flow sensors on the trunk (likely heat-pulse probes) stream data to light elements in a vine-like sculpture; commissioned by Ruinart.
works.method_zh: 树干上的液流传感器（可能是热脉冲探针）把数据传给藤蔓状雕塑中的灯光元件；由 Ruinart 委托。

works.title: Origin
works.description: A cacao tree in Indonesia fitted with sensors streams how it drinks, grows and breathes to its digital-twin sculpture in China, where the data become movement, rhythm and light.
works.description_zh: 印度尼西亚一棵装有传感器的可可树，把它喝水、生长和呼吸的数据实时传到中国的“数字孪生”雕塑，在那里转化为运动、节奏和光。
works.idea_en: Connect a consumer to the living plant behind a food product, across the supply chain, in real time.
works.idea_zh: 跨越供应链，把消费者与食物背后那棵活着的植物实时连接起来。
works.method: Environmental and plant sensors on a cacao tree send live data over the network to a kinetic light sculpture; made with the Indonesian Coffee and Cocoa Research Institute (ICCRI).
works.method_zh: 可可树上的环境与植物传感器通过网络把实时数据发送给一件动态灯光雕塑；与印尼咖啡可可研究所（ICCRI）合作。

works.title: Solaris
works.description: A visitor wearing an EEG headset moves two liquids, a ferrofluid and a fluorescent fluid, inside a sphere through magnets, so brain activity and mood become visible as shifting surfaces.
works.description_zh: 观众戴上脑电头戴设备，通过磁铁带动球体内的两种液体（磁流体和荧光液体），让脑活动和情绪变成不断变化的液面。
works.idea_en: Map inner states onto a living-looking material so people see their mind as matter.
works.idea_zh: 把内在状态映射到一种看起来像活物的材料上，让人看到自己的心智化为物质。
works.method: An Emotiv EPOC headset sends EEG data via OSC and Pure Data to Arduino-controlled motors and a permanent magnet; made with Julia Borovaya and Edward Rakhmanov, neurophysiology advice by Prof. Alexander Kaplan.
works.method_zh: Emotiv EPOC 头戴设备通过 OSC 和 Pure Data 把脑电数据传给由 Arduino 控制的电机和永磁体；与 Julia Borovaya、Edward Rakhmanov 合作，神经生理学顾问为 Alexander Kaplan 教授。

works.title: until I die
works.description: A generative synthesizer runs on batteries that use the artist's own blood as electrolyte, about 4.5 litres collected over 18 months, the last portion drawn during the opening.
works.description_zh: 一台生成式合成器由以艺术家自己的血液为电解液的电池供电，血液在 18 个月里陆续采集，共约 4.5 升，最后一份在开幕时当场抽取。
works.idea_en: Make an instrument that literally runs on the maker's vitality.
works.idea_zh: 做一件真正靠创作者生命力运转的乐器。
works.method: Five batteries of copper and aluminium electrodes in diluted, preserved blood give about 3 V, powering an Axoloti sound module and speaker.
works.method_zh: 五组以铜和铝为电极、浸在稀释并防腐处理过的血液中的电池，产生约 3 伏电压，为 Axoloti 声音模块和扬声器供电。

works.title: Hydra Reminiscence
works.description: A sound performance in which live signals generated with a Hydra, the freshwater polyp known for regeneration, are mixed with recordings made while its body regrew and with the sound of the Danube.
works.description_zh: 一场声音表演：用淡水水螅（以再生能力著称）实时产生的信号，与它身体再生期间录下的声音以及多瑙河的水声混合。
works.idea_en: Listen to a biologically 'immortal' animal to question the human wish to prolong life.
works.idea_zh: 聆听一种生物学意义上“永生”的动物，反思人类延长寿命的愿望。
works.method: A DIY biology setup in the Hackteria tradition with a Theremidi Orchestra 'Micronoise' device turns the polyp's activity under a microscope into sound (likely via electrodes or optical sensing); made at Stadtwerkstatt during Ars Electronica 2014.
works.method_zh: 沿用 Hackteria 的 DIY 生物学方法，借助 Theremidi Orchestra 的“Micronoise”设备，把显微镜下水螅的活动转化为声音（可能通过电极或光学感测）；2014 年林茨电子艺术节期间在 Stadtwerkstatt 完成。

works.title: Aurelia 1+Hz / Proto Viva Sonification
works.description: A 20-minute audiovisual performance with live moon jellyfish, whose movements in an aquarium are tracked and sonified on stage.
works.description_zh: 一场 20 分钟的视听表演，舞台上水族箱里活的海月水母的运动被追踪并转化为声音。
works.idea_en: Perform with a jellyfish as a co-player, to rehearse cohabitation between species.
works.idea_zh: 把水母当作共同演奏者，演练物种之间的共处。
works.method: Video tracking of Aurelia aurita drives sound synthesis and projection in real time; technical support by Slavko Glamočanin; honorary mention at Prix Ars Electronica 2016 (Interactive Art+).
works.method_zh: 对海月水母的视频追踪实时驱动声音合成和投影；技术支持 Slavko Glamočanin；获 2016 年 Prix Ars Electronica 互动艺术+ 类荣誉提名。

works.title: Oscillatorium – Living Systems Oscillation
works.description: An installation of objects with living plants that act as natural oscillators; when visitors engage with them, embedded sound systems mix natural and synthetic sounds.
works.description_zh: 一件由含活体植物的物件组成的装置，植物被当作天然振荡器；观众与之互动时，内嵌的声音系统混合出自然声与合成声。
works.idea_en: Treat living plants as analog oscillators, like components in a synthesizer.
works.idea_zh: 把活植物当作模拟振荡器，就像合成器里的元件。
works.method: Bioelectric oscillations of plants are picked up and fed into analog circuits (likely electrode-based biosonification) that respond to visitors' touch and proximity; shown at KIBLIX and MFRU 2015.
works.method_zh: 植物的生物电振荡被采集并送入模拟电路（可能是基于电极的生物声化），电路对观众的触碰和靠近作出反应；在 KIBLIX 和 MFRU 2015 展出。

works.title: Alt-C
works.description: Electricity from plant microbial fuel cells powers a single-board computer that mines cryptocurrency, while a neural network predicts mining yield from the weather and plans to buy land to plant more.
works.description_zh: 植物微生物燃料电池发出的电为一台挖加密货币的单板电脑供电，同时一个神经网络根据天气预测挖矿收益，并计划用收益购买土地种更多植物。
works.idea_en: Make money literally grow on plants, to question what happens when ecosystems become financial infrastructure.
works.idea_zh: 让钱真的“长在植物上”，追问生态系统变成金融基础设施会怎样。
works.method: Root exudates from photosynthesising plants feed soil bacteria that release electrons between electrodes; the current runs a mining rig, and a neural network trained on UK weather forecasts steers reinvestment.
works.method_zh: 进行光合作用的植物根系分泌物喂养土壤细菌，细菌在电极之间释放电子；电流驱动挖矿设备，一个以英国天气预报训练的神经网络决定再投资策略。

works.title: Temporary PhotoElectric Digestopians (Lab Series)
works.description: A series of participatory labs around a table where people build dye-sensitised solar cells from edible ingredients such as Aronia berry juice, then test and taste them.
works.description_zh: 一系列围绕餐桌展开的参与式工作坊：参与者用野樱莓汁等可食用材料制作染料敏化太阳能电池，然后测试并品尝它们。
works.idea_en: Make a solar cell you can eat, so energy technology becomes something grown and shared at the table.
works.idea_zh: 做一块可以吃的太阳能电池，让能源技术变成在餐桌上种出来、分享的东西。
works.method: Anthocyanin dyes from Aronia melanocarpa sensitise titanium dioxide cells that convert light into tiny currents (under 0.1% efficiency); 14 labs held across Europe since 2010.
works.method_zh: 来自黑果腺肋花楸（Aronia melanocarpa）的花青素染料敏化二氧化钛电池，把光转化为微弱电流（效率低于 0.1%）；自 2010 年起在欧洲举办了 14 场工作坊。

works.title: Prpl Vlvt (Troping Turner)
works.description: A bio-solar panel that copies J. M. W. Turner's painting 'Snow Storm' uses dyes from the Aronia plant and its endophytic bacteria to turn sunlight into electricity that lights the original painting.
works.description_zh: 一块仿照透纳画作《暴风雪》的生物太阳能板，用野樱莓植物及其内生细菌产生的染料把阳光转化为电，再用这电去照亮原画。
works.idea_en: Let a plant and its microbes power the viewing of a human masterpiece.
works.idea_zh: 让一种植物和它的微生物为观看人类名作提供电力。
works.method: Natural colourants from Aronia m. 'Babe' and bacteria living in its tissues sensitise dye solar cells arranged as the painting; developed with physicists and microbiologists at Aalto University (Janne Halme).
works.method_zh: 野樱莓品种“Babe”及其组织内细菌产生的天然色素用于敏化按画作排列的染料太阳能电池；与阿尔托大学物理学家和微生物学家（Janne Halme 等）合作开发。

works.title: Small Work for Robot and Insects
works.description: A hexapod robot tries to establish a dialogue with a colony of live crickets, composing 'sentences' of movements, lights and sounds and learning which ones the crickets answer.
works.description_zh: 一个六足机器人尝试与一群活蟋蟀建立对话，用动作、灯光和声音组成“句子”，并学习哪些句子能得到蟋蟀的回应。
works.idea_en: Let the insects decide: the machine must earn their participation.
works.idea_zh: 让昆虫来决定：机器必须赢得它们的参与。
works.method: A neural network called Dharmai analyses cricket song, picks responses from 18 motions, 7 light sequences and 32 sounds, and refines its vocabulary from the crickets' reactions.
works.method_zh: 名为 Dharmai 的神经网络分析蟋蟀鸣声，从 18 种动作、7 种灯光序列和 32 种声音中挑选回应，并根据蟋蟀的反应不断完善“词汇”。

works.title: Fish, Plant, Rack
works.description: A rail-mounted robot tends hydroponic plants while learning how to behave from the electric pulses of an elephantnose fish, and shows the fish video of the plants from its own point of view.
works.description_zh: 一个装在导轨上的机器人照料水培植物，同时从象鼻鱼的电脉冲中学习如何行动，并把自己视角下的植物影像播放给鱼看。
works.idea_en: Build a three-way loop of fish, robot and plants and ask whether the fish notices its effect.
works.idea_zh: 搭建鱼、机器人和植物的三方回路，追问鱼能否察觉自己的影响。
works.method: Electrodes in the aquarium pick up the electrolocation pulses of Gnathonemus petersii, which the AI system Dharmai (by Brian Lee Yung Rowe) interprets as parameters for the robot's actions and emotive signals.
works.method_zh: 水族箱中的电极采集象鼻鱼（Gnathonemus petersii）的电定位脉冲，由 Brian Lee Yung Rowe 开发的 AI 系统 Dharmai 解读为机器人动作和“情绪”信号的参数。

works.title: Autoinducer_Ph-1 (cross-cultural chemistry)
works.description: A robotic rice-farming installation whose arms decide whether to fertilise a rice paddy based on the state of the symbiosis between the water fern Azolla and the cyanobacterium Anabaena.
works.description_zh: 一件机器人水稻种植装置：机械臂根据满江红（Azolla）与鱼腥藻（Anabaena）共生关系的状态，决定是否给稻田施肥。
works.idea_en: Let a microbial symbiosis, read through software, run an agricultural machine.
works.idea_zh: 让一段经软件解读的微生物共生关系来操控农业机器。
works.method: Azolla-Anabaena cultures are monitored by video microscope and sensors, a software 'bacterium' (Generalized Cellular Signaling System) interacts with the data as symbiont or parasite, and the outcome drives two robot arms; made with Brian Lee Yung Rowe.
works.method_zh: 视频显微镜和传感器监测满江红与鱼腥藻培养物，一个软件“细菌”（通用细胞信号系统 GCS）以共生者或寄生者的身份与数据互动，结果驱动两只机械臂；与 Brian Lee Yung Rowe 合作。

works.title: The Great Work of the Metal Lover
works.description: An alchemical bioreactor in which a metal-tolerant bacterium turns toxic gold chloride into 24-karat gold, shown live through a microscope and in gilded electron-microscope prints.
works.description_zh: 一个炼金术式的生物反应器：耐金属细菌把有毒的氯化金转化为 24K 金，过程通过显微镜直播，并以镀金的电子显微镜图像呈现。
works.idea_en: Re-enact alchemy with a microbe, so a metabolism performs the transmutation.
works.idea_zh: 用微生物重演炼金术，让新陈代谢完成“点石成金”。
works.method: Cupriavidus metallidurans grows in a custom glass bioreactor with a CO2/H2 atmosphere and precipitates gold from AuCl3; SEM images guide gold-leaf application; made with microbiologist Kazem Kashefi.
works.method_zh: Cupriavidus metallidurans 在充有二氧化碳和氢气的定制玻璃生物反应器中生长，从氯化金中析出金；扫描电镜图像指导金箔的贴附；与微生物学家 Kazem Kashefi 合作。

works.title: ReBioGeneSys – Origins of Life
works.description: A self-running installation that combines origin-of-life experiments, from Miller-Urey sparks to freeze-thaw cycles, into minimal chemical ecosystems meant to produce self-organising molecules and perhaps protocells.
works.description_zh: 一件自主运行的装置，把米勒-尤里放电、冻融循环等生命起源实验组合成最小化学生态系统，试图产生自组织分子，甚至原始细胞。
works.idea_en: Build a sculpture that can, in principle, evolve its own chemistry toward life.
works.idea_zh: 做一件原则上能让自己的化学向生命演化的雕塑。
works.method: Automated glassware applies electrical discharge, heat, UV and freeze-thaw cycles to prebiotic mixtures, with selection steps built into the process; a collaboration with physiologist Robert Root-Bernstein.
works.method_zh: 自动化玻璃器皿对前生命化学混合物施加放电、加热、紫外和冻融循环，并在流程中加入筛选步骤；与生理学家 Robert Root-Bernstein 合作。

works.title: [ir]reverent: Miracles on Demand
works.description: A bio-incubator shaped like a Catholic monstrance grows Serratia marcescens on a Eucharist host, making the bread 'bleed' in two days, as historical blood miracles did.
works.description_zh: 一个形如天主教圣体光座的生物培养箱，在圣饼上培养黏质沙雷氏菌，两天内让圣饼“流血”，重现历史上的“血迹神迹”。
works.idea_en: Show that a microbe could have written chapters of religious history, and put it on demand.
works.idea_zh: 揭示一种微生物可能改写过宗教史，并让“神迹”可以按需发生。
works.method: Micro-droplets of S. marcescens culture are dispensed onto a host inside a temperature-controlled incubator where the red pigment prodigiosin develops.
works.method_zh: 在温控培养箱内，把黏质沙雷氏菌培养液微滴点到圣饼上，红色色素灵菌红素随之生成。
keywords: Prix Ars Electronica Artificial Intelligence & Life Art 2019

works.title: Shadows from the Walls of Death
works.description: A performance series that re-synthesises Paris Green, a toxic arsenic pigment, paints wallpaper with it, and inoculates the paint with arsenic-oxidising bacteria that turn it from green to black.
works.description_zh: 一个表演系列：重新合成有毒的砷颜料“巴黎绿”，用它绘制壁纸，再给颜料接种氧化砷的细菌，让颜色由绿转黑。
works.idea_en: Let a microbe remediate, and redraw, a poison that art once spread through homes.
works.idea_zh: 让微生物去修复、也重新描绘一种艺术曾带进千家万户的毒物。
works.method: Herminiimonas arsenicoxydans oxidises As(III) to As(V) in the Paris Green paint, shifting its colour; synthesis checked by XRD and SEM; with Rebekah Blesing and Robert Root-Bernstein.
works.method_zh: Herminiimonas arsenicoxydans 把巴黎绿颜料中的三价砷氧化为五价砷，使颜色发生变化；颜料合成经 X 射线衍射和扫描电镜验证；与 Rebekah Blesing、Robert Root-Bernstein 合作。
keywords: Prix Ars Electronica Artificial Intelligence & Life Art 2023

works.title: Estrofem! Lab
works.description: A mobile 'estrogen hack lab' of tools, protocols and engineered yeast that lets workshop participants detect estrogen in their own urine and in environmental samples.
works.description_zh: 一个可移动的“雌激素黑客实验室”，包含工具、流程和改造酵母，让工作坊参与者检测自己尿液和环境样本中的雌激素。
works.idea_en: Hand people a living sensor for the hormones in their bodies and surroundings.
works.idea_zh: 把一种活的传感器交到人们手中，用来检测自己身体和周围环境中的激素。
works.method: YES-HER yeast carrying the human estrogen receptor reports estrogen presence, and samples are prepared with DIY solid-phase extraction (cigarette filters, silica gel) and column chromatography.
works.method_zh: 携带人类雌激素受体的 YES-HER 酵母报告雌激素的存在，样本用 DIY 固相萃取（香烟滤嘴、硅胶）和柱色谱进行预处理。

works.title: The Transparent Beehive
works.description: An observation hive built like a book, with a living colony inside, fitted with microphones, cameras and climate sensors whose data are sonified and visualised to show the colony's state.
works.description_zh: 一个像书一样可翻开的观察蜂箱，里面是活的蜂群，装有麦克风、摄像头和温湿度传感器，数据被转为声音和图像，呈现蜂群状态。
works.idea_en: Make the hive readable: sound and data let people follow a colony's health day by day.
works.idea_zh: 让蜂箱变得可读：声音和数据让人能逐日跟踪蜂群的健康。
works.method: Plexiglass, wood and aluminium frames after François Huber's 1788 leaf hive carry contact microphones and webcams; audio and sensor data go through pattern recognition and AI; first installed on a Brussels rooftop.
works.method_zh: 仿照 François Huber 1788 年“书页式”蜂箱设计的有机玻璃、木材和铝框架上装有接触式麦克风和网络摄像头，音频和传感数据经过模式识别和 AI 处理；最早安装在布鲁塞尔屋顶。

works.title: The Intelligent Guerilla Beehive
works.description: A beehive for urban swarms that doubles as a biosensor: bees and bacteria report on the pollution of the foraging fields around it.
works.description_zh: 一个为城市分蜂群设计的蜂箱，同时也是生物传感器：蜜蜂和细菌报告周围采蜜区的污染状况。
works.idea_en: Design a shelter for another species that also turns it into a living monitoring technology.
works.idea_zh: 为另一个物种设计庇护所，同时让它成为活的监测技术。
works.method: A hive structure (likely 3D-printed and partly biomaterial) hosts a honeybee colony, with sensors and bacterial cultures on the shell indicating air quality; developed with scientists at JRC Ispra and UPF Barcelona.
works.method_zh: 蜂箱结构（可能由 3D 打印和部分生物材料制成）容纳一个蜂群，外壳上的传感器和细菌培养物指示空气质量；与欧盟联合研究中心（伊斯普拉）和庞培法布拉大学的科学家合作开发。

works.title: Sensorial Skin: L'Origine du Monde
works.description: A cyanobacterial biofilm grown as the outer skin of a beehive changes colour when fine-dust pollution passes a threshold, turning the hive's shell into a pollution display.
works.description_zh: 一层作为蜂箱外皮培养的蓝藻生物膜，在细颗粒物污染超过阈值时改变颜色，让蜂箱外壳成为污染显示器。
works.idea_en: Grow a living skin that shows the state of the air by changing colour.
works.idea_zh: 培养一层活的“皮肤”，用颜色变化显示空气状态。
works.method: Photosynthetic cyanobacteria in a biofilm respond to stress from atmospheric particles with visible changes in pigment and texture; a STARTS residency project.
works.method_zh: 生物膜中的光合蓝藻在大气颗粒物造成的胁迫下，色素和质地出现可见变化；为 STARTS 驻留项目。

works.title: Moon Goose Analogue: Lunar Migration Bird Facility
works.description: The artist raised eleven geese imprinted on her as their mother, named them after astronauts, trained them to fly and housed them in a moon-analogue habitat operated from a control room in the gallery.
works.description_zh: 艺术家把 11 只鹅养大，让它们把她印随为“母亲”，以宇航员的名字命名，训练它们飞行，并把它们安置在一个类月球的模拟栖息地，由展厅里的控制室远程操作。
works.idea_en: Use imprinting as an interface: the artist becomes part of the animals' world to rehearse a fiction.
works.idea_zh: 把印随当作界面：艺术家成为动物世界的一部分，一起演练一个虚构故事。
works.method: Geese were imprinted from hatching and trained on expeditions; live cameras and controls connect the remote habitat to a gallery control room; commissioned by FACT Liverpool and Arts Catalyst.
works.method_zh: 鹅从孵化起就对艺术家形成印随并参加训练远征；实时摄像头和控制系统把远方的栖息地与展厅控制室连接起来；由利物浦 FACT 与 Arts Catalyst 委托。

works.title: One Tree ID – How to Become a Tree for Another Tree
works.description: The volatile organic compounds of one Himalayan cedar are measured and turned into a perfume, so a person wearing it may take part in the chemical conversation between trees.
works.description_zh: 测量一棵喜马拉雅雪松释放的挥发性有机化合物，并把它调成香水；人涂上后，或许就能加入树与树之间的化学对话。
works.idea_en: Enter a plant's communication channel by wearing its chemical identity.
works.idea_zh: 通过“穿上”一棵树的化学身份，进入植物的交流通道。
works.method: Chamber measurements of roots, stem and needles identified over 100 VOCs, which were recomposed by a perfumer; made with Birgit Piechulla and Uta Effmert (University of Rostock).
works.method_zh: 对根、树干和针叶分别做气室测量，识别出 100 多种挥发性有机化合物，再由调香师重新调配；与罗斯托克大学的 Birgit Piechulla 和 Uta Effmert 合作。
keywords: Prix Ars Electronica Artificial Intelligence & Life Art 2019

works.title: Data Flower Shop
works.description: A pop-up flower shop run as a biological data centre: visitors had their files converted into DNA sequences, watched lab techniques for putting that DNA into a plant, and left with an encoded plant and a kit to send a sample back for reading.
works.description_zh: 一家以生物数据中心方式运营的快闪花店：访客的文件被转换成 DNA 序列，观看把 DNA 放进植物的实验方法，最后带走一株“存有数据”的植物，以及一个可寄回样本读取数据的工具包。
works.idea_en: Replace the server with a houseplant, so owning and caring for data becomes caring for a living thing.
works.idea_zh: 用一盆植物代替服务器，让拥有和照料数据变成照料一个活物。
works.method: Digital files (JPEG, MP3) were translated from binary into A, C, G, T sequences for synthetic DNA; on-site 'data florists' and a lab scientist demonstrated plant transformation methods, likely as a staged service rather than full encoding for every visitor.
works.method_zh: 把数字文件（JPEG、MP3）从二进制转译为合成 DNA 的 A、C、G、T 序列；现场由“数据花艺师”和实验室科学家演示植物转化方法，很可能是一种表演化的服务，而非为每位访客完成真实编码。

works.title: Data Garden
works.description: An installation of plants whose DNA holds encoded messages; a liquid sample is loaded into a nanopore sequencer on site and the decoded texts, images and sounds are displayed in the space.
works.description_zh: 一座由植物组成的装置，植物 DNA 中存有编码信息；现场把液体样本放入纳米孔测序仪，解码出的文字、图像和声音在空间中呈现。
works.idea_en: A data centre can be a garden that is read by sequencing instead of switched on.
works.idea_zh: 数据中心可以是一座花园，通过测序来读取，而不是通电开机。
works.method: Data were encoded into synthetic DNA carried by plants and read back in real time with portable nanopore sequencing (likely Oxford Nanopore MinION), then decoded to files.
works.method_zh: 数据被编码进植物携带的合成 DNA，再用便携式纳米孔测序仪（可能是 Oxford Nanopore MinION）实时读取并解码为文件。

works.title: Urban Data Forest
works.description: A speculative plan for The Hague in 2050 in which trees and shrubs store public archives and citizens' personal data in their DNA, as a 'Breathing Museum' and neighbourhood 'Living Archives'.
works.description_zh: 一个面向 2050 年海牙的思辨方案：树木和灌木在 DNA 中保存公共档案和市民的个人数据，形成“会呼吸的博物馆”和社区“活档案”。
works.idea_en: Imagine city greenery as infrastructure that both captures carbon and keeps memory.
works.idea_zh: 把城市绿化想象成既固碳又保存记忆的基础设施。
works.method: Architectural visualisation and site research based on plant DNA data storage via synthetic biology; the data-storing forest is proposed, not built.
works.method_zh: 基于合成生物学植物 DNA 数据存储的建筑可视化与场地研究；这片存储数据的森林是提案，尚未建成。

works.title: The Living Language Project
works.description: Paenibacillus vortex bacteria are grown in the shape of Paleo-Hebrew letters, and their spreading colonies slowly morph the ancient letters toward modern Hebrew forms in Petri dishes.
works.description_zh: 在培养皿中把 Paenibacillus vortex 细菌接种成古希伯来字母的形状，菌落不断扩展，让古老字母慢慢演变为现代希伯来字形。
works.idea_en: Let a living organism, not a type designer, write the missing evolution of an alphabet.
works.idea_zh: 让一种活的生物，而不是字体设计师，写出一套字母缺失的演化史。
works.method: Pattern-forming Paenibacillus vortex was inoculated as letterforms on nutrient agar with controlled nutrients and conditions, and its growth was time-lapse filmed; developed with Eshel Ben-Jacob's lab at Tel Aviv University.
works.method_zh: 把会形成图案的 Paenibacillus vortex 按字母形状接种在营养琼脂上，控制营养与培养条件，并用延时摄影记录其生长；与特拉维夫大学 Eshel Ben-Jacob 实验室合作完成。

works.title: Ocular Revision
works.description: A circular electrophoresis rig pulls DNA outward from the centre, so the bands slowly form images of Earth's hemispheres instead of the usual barcode-like strips.
works.description_zh: 一个圆形电泳装置把 DNA 从中心向外拉动，让条带慢慢形成地球两个半球的图像，而不是常见的条形码状条带。
